card.hook: Here's a fun twist: you're not going to Lokrum, you're looking at it. From a cliff terrace outside the Old Town wall, the island sits out on the water like a calm green hill.
card.stand_here: Head through the small doorway in the south wall to Buža Bar, on the cliff terrace outside the city wall. Face south-east and Lokrum is across the water.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so the island has open sea around it. Then try 2x-5x (depends on your phone) to bring it closer. Save zoom 0.5x for when you want the cliff edge and lots of sky.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the horizon on the lower line and Lokrum on a side third, so the sea gives it room.
card.best_time: Go at sunset, when guides mention golden light. Buža Bar is only open in spring and summer, so check before you go.
card.selfie_here: On the Buža Bar terrace the island stays in the frame behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x if your phone has it, and let Lokrum peek over your shoulder. The lookout post on the city walls is another spot with Lokrum as a clear backdrop.
card.rules_and_safety: Rocks can get slippery, especially after heavy rain, so take care. The terrace is free to enter, but you may need to buy a drink to get a seat.
card.challenge: Take one shot where Lokrum is a tiny green shape with loads of sea and sky around it. Make it look like your own private island.
card.good_to_know: A Benedictine abbey was founded on Lokrum in 1023, and in 1859 Archduke Maximilian had a mansion and garden laid out there. Fort Royal, built under French rule, stands on the highest point, 96 metres above the sea. Maximilian's peacocks still live on the island.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head through the small doorway in the south wall to Buža Bar, on the cliff terrace outside the city wall. Face south-east and Lokrum is across the water.

The Iron Throne photo spot is not a landmark-behind selfie, so I excluded it.

card.hook: Here's a funny thing about the Dubrovnik city walls: from up on top you can't actually see them. To get the whole stone circuit in one shot, you head outside and look up.
card.stand_here: Stand on the stairs of Skalini Dr. Marka Foteza, on the climb up to Fort Lovrijenac, outside the walls. Face south-east and the walls and Old Town are in front of you, with the West Harbour in the same frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze the walls, the terracotta roofs and the harbour into one picture. Then try 1x for a calmer, less stretched look. If your phone has 2x or 5x, use it to pick out a single tower or a stretch of wall.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the walls, then slide the brightness down a touch so the pale stone and the sky both keep their detail.
card.best_time: Early morning or later in the afternoon is usually calmer, with softer light. Midday in summer is the busiest and the harshest, so expect company on the steps.
card.selfie_here: Try the Buža Bar terrace on the cliff below the walls. Go through the small doorway in the south wall and down the stone steps, then turn so the wall is behind you and the sea is below. Use the front camera at 0.5x and let the wall and Lokrum Island fill the background.
card.ask_someone: Stand outside the walls just past Pile Gate and ask a passer-by to frame you against the walls.
card.rules_and_safety: The limestone on the walls is slippery in places, so wear soft-soled shoes. The stairs are outside the ticketed walls circuit, but walking the walls needs a ticket and they close before sunset, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take the same shot from three different steps and see which one gives you the most harbour.
card.good_to_know: The walls run for about 1,940 metres in one unbroken stone circuit and rise to roughly 25 metres at their highest. Most of what you see was built between the 13th and 17th centuries. They joined UNESCO's World Heritage list together with the Old Town in 1979.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the stairs of Skalini Dr. Marka Foteza, on the climb up to Fort Lovrijenac, outside the walls. Face south-east and the walls and Old Town are in front of you, with the West Harbour in the same frame.

selfie_spots.why: The city wall fills the background while the open Adriatic and Lokrum Island sit beyond the railing, so it is hard to take a bad selfie here.

card.hook: Most people shoot Banje Beach from the sand and end up with a foreground full of strangers' sunhats. Climb up to the street instead and the whole scene lines up: pebbles, sea, the Old Town, and Lokrum Island closing the frame.
card.stand_here: Stand on Frana Supila, at the top of the stairs that lead down to Banje Beach. Face the water so you're looking down onto the pebbles, with the Old Town and Lokrum Island behind them.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the view down onto the beach. Go to 0.5x to fit the beach, the Old Town and Lokrum into one frame, then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out Lokrum or the Old Town walls.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the sea's horizon on the upper or lower line, with the beach filling the bottom of the frame.
card.best_time: Early morning is the calmest, especially in July and August when cruise day-trippers fill the beach. In winter the sunbeds and bars are removed, so the picture looks tidier.
card.selfie_here: Climb the steps about halfway up from the sand towards the road. It's a raised spot with the beach below and the Old Town behind. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and hold your phone a little high so the view fits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by on the raised sidewalk right above Banje Beach to take your photo, so they can fit you in with the whole sweep of sand and water below.
card.rules_and_safety: The water is shallow at the entry point and then deepens quickly, so keep an eye on young children. If you try the low angle at the east end of the beach, the rocks may be slippery.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot with a perfectly straight horizon, then one close shot where Lokrum is the star. Bonus points if no stranger's head sneaks in.
card.good_to_know: Banje is Dubrovnik's pebble beach, just outside the Old Town. The viewpoint is on a public street, but the beach below has paid sunbed and bar areas, and the free strip is narrow. The views from above are good all along the beach, so walk a little to either side for a slightly different angle.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Frana Supila, at the top of the stairs that lead down to Banje Beach. Face the water so you're looking down onto the pebbles, with the Old Town and Lokrum Island behind them.

card.hook: Walk down Stradun and the whole street seems to point at one thing: a pale Baroque church with three statues waving from the roofline. It's the easiest 'wow' shot in the Old Town.
card.stand_here: Stand at the west end of Stradun, the long limestone street, and look east toward St Blaise's Church. It sits centred at the far end, with the facade and dome straight ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to catch the whole street leading to the church. Then try 2x to pull the facade and dome closer and make the street look squeezed together. Save 0.5x for Luža Square, when you want the column and the church in one frame.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the church on the centre line so the street edges lead into it, and keep the phone level so the buildings don't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, when the street is quieter. Midday and the 3 February Feast of St Blaise procession are the busiest times, so skip them if you want a clear frame.
card.selfie_here: Climb the broad church steps on Luža Square, turn to face the square, and let the facade sit behind you. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x if your phone has it, so the church fits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back on Stradun facing Luža Square, so the church is centred behind you while you pose in front of it.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working place of worship. Photography inside is discouraged and flash is generally discouraged too, so keep your best shots for the outside.
card.challenge: Find all three statues on the roofline, Saint Blaise in the middle with Faith and Hope either side, and get them in one shot with you pointing at them.
card.good_to_know: The church is dedicated to Saint Blaise, patron saint of Dubrovnik and protector of the independent Republic of Ragusa. The medieval church burned down in 1706. The Venetian architect and sculptor Marino Gropelli built the Baroque one you see today, finished in 1715.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the west end of Stradun, the long limestone street, and look east toward St Blaise's Church. It sits centred at the far end, with the facade and dome straight ahead of you.

card.hook: Pile Gate is busy for most of the day, so you won't get a people-free shot, but the best view here is from above the crowd anyway. Climb up and Stradun's pale stone street opens out below you.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the subject, on the wall walk directly above Pile Gate (Dubrovačke Gradske Zidine). Face down Stradun, the limestone street running away from you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the Stradun view, which keeps the street and facades looking natural. Tap 2x or higher (depends on your phone) to pick out the Franciscan dome, and use 0.5x for the gate and its bridge if you're standing close.
card.make_it_pop: Tap on the pale street, then slide the brightness down a touch so the stone doesn't turn white.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, at opening, before the crowds arrive. If you can't, use the people as scale in your street view and take a few frames in a row.
card.selfie_here: Try the stone bridge just outside the gate, with the gate arch behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x so the arch and walls fit over your shoulder. This spot is our best guess, so check the view on the ground.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in Brsalje Square, the open square outside the gate, while you pose on the stone bridge so they can photograph the outer arch and bridge.
card.rules_and_safety: Expect steps and uneven surfaces in and around the gate. The wall walk needs a paid walls ticket, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one Stradun shot with the street running dead straight down a gridline, and see if you can sneak the Franciscan dome into the corner.
card.good_to_know: Pile Gate is a western entrance to Dubrovnik's old town, where the city walls meet the approach from outside. Stradun, the main street, begins just inside it. Pile Bay on the harbour side gives a different view, with the old town walls behind a pier.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the subject, on the wall walk directly above Pile Gate (Dubrovačke Gradske Zidine). Face down Stradun, the limestone street running away from you.

card.hook: Look down from the walls and Stradun turns into one long, bright stripe between the rooftops, like someone laid a pale ribbon through the Old Town. It's neat enough to make you feel tidier just by looking at it.
card.stand_here: Stand on the elevated section of the city walls just above the gate stairs at Vrata od Pila (Pile Gate), and face east down the street. The street lies about 100 metres to the east of the gate.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the straight-down view of the whole street. Go to zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the rooftops and the far end, or zoom 0.5x to fit in more of the gate and walls. At 0.5x the edges of the frame can look a bit stretched.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and run the street along the centre line so both rows of rooftops balance, then tap the street and drag the slider to darker so the pale stone doesn't wash out.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or after dark, when the street is emptier and the stone has a nice sheen. After dark, switch on night mode and rest your elbows on the wall to keep the phone steady.
card.selfie_here: Try Big Onofrio's Fountain, on the small open square just inside Pile Gate. Use the front camera, stand slightly away from the fountain, and keep the stonework and the start of Stradun over your shoulder. For a couple photo, Luža Square at the other end of the street, near Sponza Palace and the Bell Tower, is a guide's pick.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to climb the stairs just inside Pile Gate and stand at the top, while you stand on Stradun below with Onofrio's Fountain and the Franciscan Monastery dome in view.
card.rules_and_safety: The polished limestone can get slippery, so wear shoes with good grip, especially after rain. The street itself is pedestrian-only, but the city walls above Pile Gate need a ticket, so check the official site for opening times before you go.
card.challenge: Can you get the street perfectly down the centre line, with both rows of rooftops matching like a mirror? Take three tries and keep the best one.
card.good_to_know: Stradun is a limestone-paved pedestrian street about 300 metres long, running from Pile Gate in the west to Ploče Gate in the east. The ground was once a marshy channel, reclaimed in the 13th century. Most of what you see today dates from after the 1667 earthquake, when the Republic of Ragusa set rules for how houses were built. That's why every frontage has the same pattern: a shop under a rounded arch, with living rooms above.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the elevated section of the city walls just above the gate stairs at Vrata od Pila (Pile Gate), and face east down the street. The street lies about 100 metres to the east of the gate.

selfie_spots.why: It is the most recognisable spot where the street begins, and a page advises standing a little back from the fountain to include the beginning of Stradun behind it.

card.hook: Walk down the Stradun and the Rector's Palace shows up at the far end, like the street planned it. It's a row of arches that looks great on a phone, and it has survived a fire, an explosion and an earthquake.
card.stand_here: Stand in Luža, the square the palace faces, and face the arched front, which lies to the south-east of you. Step back until the whole facade fits, with the Cathedral and Old Town buildings behind it.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole facade. If you're close and the arches won't fit, tap 0.5x. Then try 2x or more (depends on your phone) for a single arch or a carved capital.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the columns up with the vertical lines so the arches stand up straight.
card.best_time: Evening or night, when the palace is lit up and the stonework glows. Sunset is a good shot too.
card.selfie_here: Try the worn stone seats under the arches of the palace's entrance corridor. Use the front camera, tap 0.5x if you want more arches in, and keep the palace architecture behind your shoulder. Guides call this shaded corridor a popular photo spot, but check the seats on the spot first.
card.ask_someone: Ask your helper to stand in Luža, across from the palace's arched front so the whole building fits, while you stand in front of the arches.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos without flash are allowed inside the palace, but some rooms may restrict photography, so look for signs. The interior is a ticketed museum, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole front, then hunt for a single carved capital and see if you can make it look like a postcard.
card.good_to_know: The Rector's Palace was the seat of government of the Republic of Ragusa, the old city-state of Dubrovnik, from the 14th century until 1808. A fire in 1435, a gunpowder explosion in 1463 and the earthquake of 1667 each led to rebuilding, which is why you see Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque touches together. Since 1872 part of it has housed the history department of the Museum of Dubrovnik.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Luža, the square the palace faces, and face the arched front, which lies to the south-east of you. Step back until the whole facade fits, with the Cathedral and Old Town buildings behind it.

card.hook: Picture a pale stone fort that seems to grow straight out of a cliff, 37 metres above the sea, with the water all around it. Locals nicknamed it "Dubrovnik's Gibraltar", and from across the bay you'll see why.
card.stand_here: Stand in Park Gradac, across the bay from Fort Lovrijenac, and face south-east. From here the fort sits with the sea and the Old Town walls behind it.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to catch the fort, the bay and the Old Town walls together. Then try 2x or 5x (depends on your phone) to bring in the terraces and the gate. Skip 0.5x unless you want lots of sky, because the fort ends up looking small.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and put the fort on one of the vertical lines with water filling the bottom of the frame, then tap the fort and drag the slider to make it a little darker so the pale stone keeps its detail.
card.selfie_here: Try the landing at the top of the last flight of stairs just before the fort's entrance gate. Use the front camera, turn so the fortress is over your shoulder, and try 0.5x if your phone has it to fit more in. One guide says you can take photos there without a ticket.
card.ask_someone: For a shot of you with the fort in view, ask a passer-by at the "Houses and Fortress View" lookout on Ul. don Frana Bulića, on the hillside west of the fort next to a parking lot.
card.rules_and_safety: One guide warns that the viewpoint on the fort's grounds is steep with a fairly small ledge, so take care there. Going into the fort needs a ticket, so check the official site for prices and opening hours.
card.challenge: Get two shots from the same spot: a wide one at 1x with plenty of water, then a close one at 5x of just the gate, and see which one your friends like better.
card.good_to_know: The people of Dubrovnik built the fort in just three months, say the chronicles, to stop Venice getting there first. Its outer walls are up to 12 metres thick, but the walls facing the city are only about 60 centimetres thick. Above the gate, a Latin inscription says liberty cannot be sold for all the gold in the world.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Park Gradac, across the bay from Fort Lovrijenac, and face south-east. From here the fort sits with the sea and the Old Town walls behind it.

card.hook: Stradun is one long, shiny limestone street, and it points straight at Sponza Palace like it's showing off. Let the street do the work and you'll get a good photo in about ten seconds.
card.stand_here: Stand on Placa (that's the local name for Stradun), at its eastern end, and look back at the palace. Face north and it's straight ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at 1x so the palace sits at the end of the street with the paving leading to it. Tap 2x or higher, if your phone has it, for a tighter shot of the loggia and its carvings. If you step into the courtyard, 0.5x helps you fit in the arches and columns.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, line the street up with the middle of the frame, and tap the palace, then slide it a bit darker if the pale stone looks washed out.
card.best_time: Early morning or later in the evening, when Stradun is usually quieter. Take a few shots in a row anyway, because people keep wandering through the frame.
card.selfie_here: Try Luža Square, in front of the palace doorway, with the facade behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if you can, and hold the phone a little low and wide so the building fits over your shoulder. If you get inside, the arches of the courtyard make a lovely backdrop with the columns behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to shoot from Luža Square, beside the Rector's Palace next to St. Blaise's Church, so the palace and the Clock Tower both fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Flash is restricted inside the palace and in the Memorial Room, where you should keep photography discreet. Drones aren't permitted in the Old Town. The facade has been reported under restoration, which can block the view, and the courtyard may be taken up by art exhibitions.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the paving leads your eye all the way to the palace, with not a single stranger in it. Good luck!
card.good_to_know: Sponza Palace was built between 1516 and 1522 in a mix of Gothic and Renaissance styles. Over the years it has been a customs house, mint, armoury, treasury, bank and school, and it came through the 1667 earthquake undamaged. Today it holds the Dubrovnik State Archive, with records going back to the 12th century.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Placa (that's the local name for Stradun), at its eastern end, and look back at the palace. Face north and it's straight ahead of you.

card.hook: Picture a whole walled city laid out below you like a model, red roofs, sea and an island all in one go. That's Srđ, and even a quick snap looks like you planned it.
card.stand_here: Stand at the summit by the white stone cross and Fort Imperial, right where the phone icon sits on the map. Face the walled city and the sea below, and keep the cross or a fort wall at the edge of your frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to catch the sweep of city, sea and island. Then go to 1x for a natural view, and try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Stradun, the rooftops or Lokrum.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the horizon on the top or bottom line, then tap the Old Town and slide a touch darker so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Late afternoon to early evening gives softer light and warmer colours on the city and sea, while midday can look flat and hazy. If the city lights come on at dusk, try night mode and rest your elbows on a wall to keep steady.
card.selfie_here: Try the Stone Cross lookout, at the white cross right beside and in front of Panorama restaurant. Use the front camera at 0.5x and tuck the cross or the view over your shoulder. For a quieter backdrop, head left out of the upper cable car station and cross the car park to the wide open clearing, which looks out toward the Elaphiti Islands.
card.ask_someone: At the lower cable car station just outside the walls near Pile Gate, stand by the station and ask a passer-by to step back and frame you with Srđ rising behind.
card.rules_and_safety: The zigzag hiking path has lots of loose rocks, and walking down it in the dark is a bad idea, so take the cable car down after sunset. Bring water if you hike up. The stone cross spot can get crowded at sunset.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole scene, then one close-up of a single detail like the Stradun or Lokrum, and see which one you like better.
card.good_to_know: Srđ rises to 412 metres directly behind the Old Town. Fort Imperial was built by the French in 1810 and now houses a museum about the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995). Srđ saw fierce fighting during the Siege of Dubrovnik, which gives the view real weight beyond the red roofs.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the summit by the white stone cross and Fort Imperial, right where the phone icon sits on the map. Face the walled city and the sea below, and keep the cross or a fort wall at the edge of your frame.

card.hook: In 1667 an earthquake flattened this church, and one thing walked away without a scratch: the carved doorway. It's now the star of a busy Stradun scene, with people drifting through your shot like extras.
card.stand_here: Stand near Od Sigurate, about 20 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west. The church portal is right there by the start of Stradun, near the Pile Gate.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the facade and portal in their street. If the street is too tight to fit the whole front, drop to zoom 0.5x. Then try zoom 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the Pietà and the carved figures.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the portal on one of the vertical lines and keep your phone level so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or in the evening, when Stradun is quieter. Check which way the facade is lit on the day, because strong direct sun can make the carving look harsh.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside Onofrio's Large Fountain, right in front of the church, with the church and friary facade behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x to fit more in, and hold your phone a little high.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by at the east end of Stradun to take your photo while you stand near the fountain, so the friary facade is in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos aren't allowed inside the monastery museum or the pharmacy, and flash is usually banned in the church and friary. The patio is fine for photos, but ask staff at the entrance how much the cloister allows.
card.challenge: Find the Pietà in the middle of the doorway, then catch it with St Jerome and St John the Baptist on either side and the Father Creator on top, all in one shot.
card.good_to_know: The portal was carved in 1498 in the Gothic style by the workshop of the brothers Leonard and Petar Petrović. The friary pharmacy dates from 1317 and is described as the oldest still-working pharmacy in Europe. The lower cloister has 120 columns, and every carved capital is different.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand near Od Sigurate, about 20 m east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face west. The church portal is right there by the start of Stradun, near the Pile Gate.

card.hook: Your first problem here is people, because everyone in Dubrovnik seems to wander through the one spot you've picked. Be patient, because this Baroque beauty with its big dome and a doorway flanked by four columns is worth the wait.
card.stand_here: Stand in Poljana Luža, on the west side of the square, and look across at the cathedral. You'll see its Baroque front at a slight angle, with St Blaise's Church and Orlando's Column nearby.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze the façade and the dome into one frame, since the building is big and you're close. Then try 1x for a natural look, and 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the saints in the niches and the top of the dome.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line up the building's straight vertical edges with them, so the walls don't lean over.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people. Midday sun can be harsh and the crowds thicker.
card.selfie_here: Stand in Luža Square where Stradun ends, with the cathedral's façade right behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold your arm out so the dome peeks over your shoulder. For a different angle, try under the outer arches of the Rector's Palace, with the cathedral framed in the background.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand across the square at a slight angle to the cathedral, so the whole building fits, while you pose with the façade behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos without flash are allowed in the cathedral nave. Photography in the Treasury is restricted or not permitted, so follow the signs and staff instructions. It's a place of worship, so expect modest dress and check the official site for visiting arrangements.
card.challenge: Can you get all four columns, the dome and one very patient saint in the same shot, with nobody's head in the way?
card.good_to_know: The 1667 earthquake destroyed the earlier churches, so work on this cathedral began in 1671 and finished in 1713. Inside, the main altar holds a triptych attributed to Titian. The cathedral is part of Dubrovnik's UNESCO World Heritage listing, and Richard the Lionheart is said to have helped pay for an early church here after surviving a shipwreck in 1192.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Poljana Luža, on the west side of the square, and look across at the cathedral. You'll see its Baroque front at a slight angle, with St Blaise's Church and Orlando's Column nearby.

card.hook: From the Pile Gate bridge, Minčeta Tower looks like a big stone drum sitting on the skyline, and it's hard to miss. Its heavy round shape makes it a very easy subject to pick out.
card.stand_here: Stand on Pile Gate bridge, on the approach to Pile Gate outside the walls, with Mount Srđ behind the tower. Face south-east and the tower should sit right in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to fit the whole tower in. Go to 2x or more (depending on your phone) for a tighter shot of the stonework. Use 0.5x only if you want lots of sky, and keep the tower away from the edges so it doesn't look stretched.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the tower, then slide the brightness down a little if the sky looks washed out, because stone keeps its detail better in a slightly darker picture.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer harsh shadows than the middle of the day.
card.selfie_here: Try the photo point on the city walls at the tower itself, or the walls above the rooftop basketball court, where the tower is nearby. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and see if you can fit the tower over your shoulder. Guides list these as photo points but don't promise the tower will be right behind you, so check your screen.
card.ask_someone: Walk out through Buža Gate, go up to the fire station, turn left and keep climbing the road until you're level with the tower, then ask a passer-by on the road to take your photo while you stand on the raised platform of the newly restored chapel opposite Minčeta.
card.rules_and_safety: Expect steep stone steps and a narrow spiral staircase at the tower. It isn't wheelchair-accessible and can be tough for anyone with mobility issues, so check local access information before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot with the tower on a gridline, then sneak in a closer one where you can count the stones.
card.good_to_know: Minčeta Tower is in Dubrovnik, and its heavy round form stands out against the sky. Include a little sky and the surroundings and you get a real sense of its scale. If visitors wander into your shot, wait for a gap, or let one or two stay in to show how big the tower is.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Pile Gate bridge, on the approach to Pile Gate outside the walls, with Mount Srđ behind the tower. Face south-east and the tower should sit right in front of you.

card.hook: You walk through Pile Gate, the crowd swirls around you, and there it is: a big round fountain with carved stone faces all the way around. Everyone stops here, so you're in good company.
card.stand_here: Stand in Poljana Paska Miličevića, just inside Pile Gate. The fountain is about 21 m to the north, so face it and step back until you can see its whole curve with the Old Town entrance and Pile Gate behind it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole fountain with the gate behind it, then try 1x for a more natural look. Go to 2x-5x (depending on your phone) for the carved masks and water spouts.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the fountain, then slide the brightness down a touch to make it a bit darker, so the bright stone and water keep their detail.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, when the square is least crowded. Blue hour on the Stradun is lovely too, so switch on night mode and tuck your elbows into your body to keep the phone steady.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, hold the phone a little higher and switch to 0.5x if your phone has it. Turn so the landmark sits over your shoulder, then take a few in a row.
card.rules_and_safety: The Stradun's limestone can be slippery when wet, so watch your footing. Some spouts may not be running, so check what's flowing before you plan a close-up.
card.challenge: Turn on Live Photos and catch a stone mask with water pouring out of its mouth. Bonus points if nobody walks through your frame.
card.good_to_know: This is the large fountain just inside Pile Gate. It has a 16-sided form with carved stone masks and water spouts running around it. The small Onofrio's Fountain near Luža Square is a different structure, so don't mix them up.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Poljana Paska Miličevića, just inside Pile Gate. The fountain is about 21 m to the north, so face it and step back until you can see its whole curve with the Old Town entrance and Pile Gate behind it.

card.hook: Most people snap this bridge from far away and get a thin grey line. Walk right underneath it instead, look up, and 38 cables fan out over your head like a giant harp.
card.stand_here: Stand on Obala Ivana Pavla II., the quay beside the bus station in Gruž, and walk a short way along it until you're directly under the bridge. Face up at the span and tilt your phone toward the pylon.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x so the pylon, the cables and the deck all squeeze into one frame. Then try 1x for a calmer, less stretched look, and 2x or 5x (if your phone has them) to pick out the top of the pylon.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the pylon on one vertical line so the cables sweep across the frame, then tap the bridge and drag the slider a little darker so the sky stays blue.
card.best_time: We don't have a confirmed best hour for this one, so go when the sky is clear and the structure isn't washed out. Take a quick test shot when you arrive and check how the light looks.
card.selfie_here: Vidikovac Lozica, the little park on the approach road just before the bridge, has the bridge and the city both in view. Use the front camera at 0.5x and check the screen to see how much bridge squeezes in over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Stand on the waterside directly beneath the bridge deck and ask a passer-by to step back along the quay and tilt up, so the whole span is framed overhead.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working road bridge, so keep clear of traffic and stay on the quay. Pedestrian access onto the deck is unclear, so check on the ground first. Wind can be strong here in storms, so look at the forecast.
card.challenge: Get the pylon on a gridline and make the cables lead the eye all the way to the top, with no wonky tilt.
card.good_to_know: The pylon is 141.5 metres tall, and the bridge is 518 metres long. It opened on 21 May 2002 and was renamed the Franjo Tuđman Bridge in 2004. The plate on the pillar still says "Most Dubrovnik", so look for it.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Obala Ivana Pavla II., the quay beside the bus station in Gruž, and walk a short way along it until you're directly under the bridge. Face up at the span and tilt your phone toward the pylon.

card.hook: Picture a fat, rounded stone fort with nothing behind it but cliffs and open sea. That's Fort Bokar, and it's a gift to your phone because the frame stays wonderfully uncluttered.
card.stand_here: Stand a short walk past the fort, and face north-west to look back at it. Bokar sits in profile to one side, with the sea and Fort Lovrijenac in the distance. You can also try the harbour side at Pile Bay, but that exact spot isn't fixed, so check the map.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the fort, the sea and Lovrijenac all in one shot. Try 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) to pull Lovrijenac closer behind the fort. Use 0.5x only if you're close and want the whole rounded wall.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the fort on one side third of the frame and let the sea fill the rest.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when it's quieter. Summer crowds can be heavy, so take two or three frames and pick the one with no heads in the corner.
card.selfie_here: Try the big stone balcony at the Mirador viewpoint overlooking Bokar Bastion, and come early to beat the crowds. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and tilt so the fort sits over your shoulder. We haven't confirmed the exact framing, so check it on the spot. Another option is the path beside Dubravka 1836, where a cement barrier runs along the edge and the fort and Lovrijenac are in view across the water.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone on the Kolorina Beach side of Pile Bay, where the kayaks are pulled up, to take your photo with Fort Bokar across the bay behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The wall-walk view needs a ticket, and entry rules for Fort Lovrijenac may apply too, so check the official site before you go. One review warns that the uphill walk to the fort isn't great if you're unsteady on your feet.
card.challenge: Get the fort off-centre, the sea filling the other half, and not a single stray head in the corner.
card.good_to_know: Fort Bokar is the rounded fort on the sea side of Dubrovnik's city walls, close to Pile Bay. Fort Lovrijenac stands out on its rock beyond it. If you only have time for one view, the wall walk gives a calmer composition.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, a short walk past the fort, and face north-west to look back at it. Bokar sits in profile to one side, with the sea and Fort Lovrijenac in the distance. You can also try the harbour side at Pile Bay, but that exact spot isn't fixed, so check the map.

card.hook: Stradun runs dead straight, and at the far end a 31-metre tower with a clock and a dome sits there like a full stop. Your eyes go straight to it, which makes this an easy photo.
card.stand_here: Stand on Stradun, the Old Town's main street, and face down the street toward the Bell Tower. It's about 278 m on foot to the south-east, at the far end of the street.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole street with the tower at the end. Then try 2x or higher, if your phone has it, to bring the clock face closer. Zoom 0.5x gives you lots of sky and the building fronts, but keep the tower in the middle so it doesn't look stretched.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the tower on the middle vertical line and keep your phone level so the buildings don't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon. The light is softer and the street is less crowded.
card.selfie_here: Try Luža Square beside Orlando's Column, where photographers reportedly set up for the view back down Stradun. Face down the street with the tower behind you, use the front camera and try 0.5x so more of the scene fits in.
card.rules_and_safety: Stradun is an open public street. Whether you can climb the tower itself is unclear, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Wait for a gap in the crowd, then catch one person walking toward the tower so everyone can see how big it is.
card.good_to_know: The tower was first built in 1444. Earthquakes damaged it and it began to lean towards Stradun, so it was taken down in 1928 and rebuilt to the original design in 1929. The bell was cast in 1506 and is struck by two green bronze figures, Maro and Baro. The ones up there now are 1929 replicas, and the originals from around 1478 are in the Cultural History Museum in the Rector's Palace.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Stradun, the Old Town's main street, and face down the street toward the Bell Tower. It's about 278 m on foot to the south-east, at the far end of the street.
